<!--

Thank you for sending a pull request! Here are some tips:

1. If this is your first time, please read our contribution guide at https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

2. Ensure you include and run the appropriate tests as part of your Pull Request.

3. In a new feature or configuration option, an update to the documentation is necessary. Everything related to the documentation is under the docs folder in the root of the repository.

4. If the Pull Request is a work in progress, make use of GitHub's "Draft PR" feature and mark it as such.

5. If you can not merge your Pull Request due to a merge conflict, Rebase it. This gets it in sync with the main branch.

6. Name your PR as "<FeatureArea>: Describe your change", e.g. Alerting: Prevent race condition. If it's a fix or feature relevant for the changelog describe the user impact in the title. The PR title is used to auto-generate the changelog for issues marked with the "add to changelog" label.

7. If your PR content should be added to the What's New document for the next major or minor release, add the **add to what's new** label to your PR. Note that you should add this label to the main PR that introduces the feature; do not add this label to smaller PRs for the feature.

-->

**What is this feature?**

[Add a brief description of what the feature or update does.]

**Why do we need this feature?**

[Add a description of the problem the feature is trying to solve.]

**Who is this feature for?**

[Add information on what kind of user the feature is for.]

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

<!--

- Automatically closes linked issue when the Pull Request is merged.

Usage: "Fixes #<issue number>", or "Fixes (paste link of issue)"

-->

Fixes #

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

Please check that:
- [ ] It works as expected from a user's perspective.
- [ ] If this is a pre-GA feature, it is behind a feature toggle.
- [ ] The docs are updated, and if this is a [notable improvement](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/#how-to-determine-if-content-belongs-in-whats-new), it's added to our [What's New](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/) doc.
pr.title: Alerting: Remove ruler from alert list view2

raw_findings.body: The menu item is displayed from the Prometheus-rule ability, but RuleActionsButtons has no rulerRule, so the ruler-only drawer condition remains false and clicking Silence produces no drawer or silence workflow.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The UI advertises an available action that silently does nothing when invoked.
raw_findings.impact: The menu item is displayed from the Prometheus-rule ability, but RuleActionsButtons has no rulerRule, so the ruler-only drawer condition remains false and clicking Silence produces no drawer or silence workflow.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new Grafana list item supplies only promRule while the existing silence rendering path still requires rulerRule.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Make the silence workflow accept the GrafanaPromRuleDTO/UID, or retain and provide the corresponding RulerGrafanaRuleDTO before exposing the Silence menu item.
raw_findings.title: Grafana list Silence action opens no drawer
raw_findings.trigger: A user with silence permissions opens More for a Grafana-managed alerting rule rendered by GrafanaRuleListItem and selects Silence notifications.

raw_findings.body: Although the Prometheus-based ability can report Delete as supported and allowed, AlertRuleMenu still requires rulerRule before rendering the Delete item, so the user cannot delete the rule from the list.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A permitted destructive operation disappears from the list UI even though its ability check succeeds.
raw_findings.impact: Although the Prometheus-based ability can report Delete as supported and allowed, AlertRuleMenu still requires rulerRule before rendering the Delete item, so the user cannot delete the rule from the list.
raw_findings.root_cause: The list migration stopped passing rulerRule without updating the menu's delete-item prerequisite.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the rulerRule-only rendering guard and invoke the delete modal using the Grafana rule identifier, or provide a compatible ruler rule before showing Delete.
raw_findings.title: Grafana list omits the Delete action
raw_findings.trigger: A user with folder delete permission opens More for a Grafana-managed rule in the list view.

raw_findings.body: The Prometheus-based ability can allow Pause, but the menu renders MenuItemPauseRule only when a Grafana ruler rule is present, so no pause or resume control is shown.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Pause/resume functionality is unavailable from the migrated list view despite being supported and authorized.
raw_findings.impact: The Prometheus-based ability can allow Pause, but the menu renders MenuItemPauseRule only when a Grafana ruler rule is present, so no pause or resume control is shown.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new list item passes only promRule while the pause menu remains coupled to rulerRule.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Adapt MenuItemPauseRule to operate on the GrafanaPromRuleDTO/identifier, or retain the ruler rule for this action and do not claim Pause support without it.
raw_findings.title: Grafana list cannot pause rules
raw_findings.trigger: A user opens More for a Grafana-managed alerting rule rendered without a ruler response and has permission to pause it.

raw_findings.body: The refactored ability calculation no longer suppresses Update, Delete, Pause, or related operations for federated rules, so the UI exposes actions that were previously blocked for immutable federated groups and those operations can fail or violate the intended rule lifecycle.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Ability results regress for federated rules and review of their mutability becomes incorrect.
raw_findings.impact: The refactored ability calculation no longer suppresses Update, Delete, Pause, or related operations for federated rules, so the UI exposes actions that were previously blocked for immutable federated groups and those operations can fail or violate the intended rule lifecycle.
raw_findings.root_cause: The refactor removed isFederatedRuleGroup handling and replaced it with an unconditional false value.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the existing federated-group detection for CombinedRule callers and carry that immutable flag into the shared ability calculation instead of hardcoding false.
raw_findings.title: Federated rules are no longer treated as immutable
raw_findings.trigger: A federated rule is evaluated through the existing useAllAlertRuleAbilities(CombinedRule) path and the user has ordinary rule update or delete permissions.

raw_findings.body: The generated link no longer carries the originating returnTo parameter, so the user is returned to the default location rather than the prior filtered/list context.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Navigation loses list filters and context when moving from the list to rule details and back.
raw_findings.impact: The generated link no longer carries the originating returnTo parameter, so the user is returned to the default location rather than the prior filtered/list context.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new list-item implementation copied the view path but dropped the prior component's returnTo URL construction.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Generate the current return location with createReturnTo() and pass it through createRelativeUrl when constructing the Grafana rule view URL.
raw_findings.title: Grafana rule links lose the originating return location
raw_findings.trigger: A user opens a Grafana rule from a filtered or otherwise non-default alert list view and then uses the rule view's return navigation.

raw_findings.body: The component's JSDoc and expectedRulesCount comments describe a Ruler request and Ruler response differences that no longer exist, misleading future changes and potentially causing the removed request dependency to be reintroduced.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Code review and maintenance decisions are based on an inaccurate description of the component's data sources.
raw_findings.impact: The component's JSDoc and expectedRulesCount comments describe a Ruler request and Ruler response differences that no longer exist, misleading future changes and potentially causing the removed request dependency to be reintroduced.
raw_findings.root_cause: The implementation removed the Ruler query without updating the surrounding loader documentation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update the loader documentation to state that it loads and polls only the Grafana Prometheus endpoint, and remove the obsolete Ruler-response explanation.
raw_findings.title: GrafanaGroupLoader documentation still claims it loads the Ruler endpoint
raw_findings.trigger: A maintainer relies on the GrafanaGroupLoader documentation after this implementation changes the loader to use only the Prometheus response.
